abstract: Recent advances in Gaussian splatting have enabled efficient and photorealistic head avatar reconstruction, yet monocular video–based or image-based methods still suffer from under-constrained geometry and texture, leading to artifacts such as blurring, stretching, and temporal instability. We present EDGAR (Efficient Diffusion-Driven Gaussian Avatar Refinement), a conditional diffusion framework designed to enhance the quality of Gaussian avatars by correcting artifacts while preserving identity fidelity. To train EDGAR, we construct EDGAR-SET, a hybrid triplet dataset composed of real-captured and synthetic-rendered samples, which simulates realistic Gaussian avatar failure cases by pairing degraded renderings with ground-truth and reference images. EDGAR refines degraded frames through a fusion block that injects identity features extracted by the self-supervised Sapiens model into a one-step diffusion backbone, enabling effective artifact removal without sacrificing efficiency. Our EDGAR model incorporates a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architecture to address diverse degradation types and severity levels. The refined multi-view renderings are subsequently used as pseudo-targets to optimize a single underlying Gaussian avatar, so that the final avatar can be rendered without applying EDGAR to every output frame. Experiments on three different Gaussian avatar reconstruction methods, each evaluated under three different settings, show improvements in both perceptual and reconstruction measures over the raw outputs and an SDEdit-style refinement baseline. In addition, cross-view evaluation demonstrates improved calibrated consistency, while tests under large yaw and open-mouth expressions verify robustness under extreme settings. These results collectively indicate a useful operating regime for recoverable appearance artifacts. The code is publicly available at EDGAR.

sections.body: The introduction says monocular and few-image Gaussian head avatars are under-constrained, which causes blurring, stretching and temporal instability. It argues that SDEdit-style diffusion refinement lacks knowledge of the target avatar and cannot reliably preserve identity. The proposed EDGAR is a conditional one-step diffusion refiner that takes a degraded frame and a reference image. Training uses EDGAR-SET, a hybrid of real NeRSemble-based and synthetic CAFCA-based triplets. A fusion block injects Sapiens identity features, and a Mixture-of-Experts module handles varied degradations. The listed contributions are the dataset, a refinement framework that distills refined 2D targets into the 3D avatar, and subject-reference and expression-aware supervision. No numbers are given in this section.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Monocular Gaussian avatars show artifacts, so EDGAR refines degraded renderings with a diffusion prior and reference identity.

sections.body: Related work covers 3DMM and implicit head reconstruction. Gaussian head avatars are split into multi-view methods, which need calibrated camera arrays, and monocular or few-image methods, which are under-constrained and show blurry textures and floating Gaussians. Generative refinement work includes GAN-based editing, SDEdit-style refinement that can cause temporal jittering and identity changes, and Difix3D+, a single-step refiner coupled with NeRF and 3DGS optimization. The authors position EDGAR as applying a related single-step strategy to animatable Gaussian head avatars. It adds paired avatar failures, subject reference and expression supervision, and shared 3D optimization, without per-frame diffusion inference. This section reports no experiments.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior refinement methods use SDEdit-style noising that can alter identity, while EDGAR adds reference features and paired supervision.

sections.body: The method has three parts. EDGAR-SET is built from NeRSemble with RGBAvatar and from CAFCA with 3DGS, yielding triplets of degraded renderings, ground-truth images and reference frames. Triplets are filtered with LPIPS, and the final set totals 400K high-resolution images. EDGAR is a conditional diffusion refiner built on SD-Turbo. Self-attention layers are updated, while residual and cross-attention layers stay frozen. A fusion block passes Sapiens features of the reference into cross-attention with a zero-initialized output. A six-expert Mixture-of-Experts routes features after the attention layers. Training combines LPIPS, l2 and Gram losses with an expression loss and a load-balancing loss. Refined multi-view renderings then supervise the Gaussian avatar with L1 and SSIM losses, without splitting or adding Gaussians.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: EDGAR-SET pairs simulated degraded renderings with ground truth and reference images, and EDGAR injects Sapiens features into a one-step diffusion model.

sections.body: Experiments cover CAP4D with 1, 4 and 8 images, RGBAvatar with 1, 4 and 8 videos, and GaussianAvatars with 8, 10 and 12 videos. Each is compared with the raw output and an SDEdit-style baseline, at unseen views. On CAP4D, EDGAR has the highest CLIP and lowest L1 at every input count, while the baseline keeps the lowest LPIPS. On RGBAvatar and GaussianAvatars, EDGAR leads all four metrics at every input count. In cross-identity reenactment, EDGAR stays just below the input avatar in CSIM, a negligible degradation, while SDEdit causes a substantial drop. Ablations show the reference image, synthetic split and expression loss have larger effects than MoE. In a user study with 15 participants, EDGAR was preferred over CAP4D in 96.67% of overall-preference choices.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Against raw inputs and SDEdit, EDGAR leads most self-reenactment metrics, and 15 participants preferred it.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes EDGAR as single-step refinement with paired avatar-failure data, subject-reference conditioning, expression-aware supervision and an auxiliary MoE module. It reports gains that depend on the starting avatar and metric, improved calibrated cross-view consistency for CAP4D and GaussianAvatars, and benefits under large yaw and open-mouth conditions. The limitations section states that EDGAR-SET keeps only structurally recoverable degradations, so severe structural errors and unobserved-region artifacts can remain. Independently refined pseudo-targets can disagree across views. Mouth interiors and translucent appearance remain challenging. Mean tWE decreased for CAP4D and RGBAvatar but increased for GaussianAvatars.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: EDGAR's gains vary by pipeline and metric, and severe structural errors in unobserved regions can remain.
